sites: Grace Medical Center A Sinai Hospital Facility

scope: Medical Center Complex, Adult Inpatient and Adult Emergency Department population.
purpose: To provide guidance for administering intravenous (IV) medications to patients eighteen (18) years of age or older, with allowance for adaptation in extenuating circumstances.

medications.considerations: Must use 0.22-micron filter with infusion.
IV push 100mg - 500mg over 1 minute

medications.areasOfUse: G: ACLS or PALS trained RN may administer in a monitored setting or emergent situation with MP present at bedside and Lifepak in place. Otherwise, should be administered by MP on non-monitored unit. CC: Nurse can administer in CC with or without MP present. E: Pushed by CC nurse or ACLS or PALS trained RN with MP at the bedside.
medications.considerations: Push rapidly over 1-2 seconds while on cardiac monitor. 1st dose: 6mg, 2nd dose: 12mg, 3rd dose no longer recommended by the 2020 American Heart Association (AHA) ACLS guidelines; doses 2 min apart. Flush immediately with 10mL NS. Brief period of asystole may be seen. RN administers in G, CC or E (please see specifics in column to the left). Patient should be on continuous cardiac monitor or EKG at time of administration. AHA recommends when Adenosine is given via a central line that the doses should be reduced to half doses.

Use standard IV tubing, insert tubing spike into vented spike adapter, then spike bottle. Do not infuse with other medications. Avoid use in Jehovah’s Witness patients as albumin is a human plasma protein. Normovolemia: infuse 5% Albumin at 2 – 10ml/min, 25% Albumin at 1- 3ml/min. Hypovolemia: infuse single dose as rapidly as possible up to 10ml/min. Do not exceed 10ml/min to prevent pulmonary edema. Monitor and notify provider for major side effects: hypersensitivity reaction, anaphylaxis, pulmonary edema, pruritis. +Grace Medical only carries albumin 25%, 50ml product
Glass container; Stable for 24 hours. Monitor VS and S/S bleeding

sourceAlerts: Page 9: Amphotericin B (non-liposomal) states ‘> concentration through central line’ without defining the higher concentration.
Pages 10–11: Calcium chloride text spans the page break and does not cleanly delimit every CRRT, push-rate, and replacement-form clause.
Page 12: Chlorpromazinee has IVPB marked while the note also discusses IV push; both routes are shown as conditional without resolving the conflict.
Page 18: Kcentra (4 Factor PCC) appears as an otherwise blank alias row immediately after the Factor II,VII,IX,X PCC entry.
Page 23: Levofloxacin is marked IVPB while its consideration text says ‘IV Push’; both routes are shown as conditional.
Page 27: Naloxone timing wording is preserved exactly and requires institutional review before reinterpretation.
Page 28: Source-visible rate units include an anomalous value; no unit was corrected silently.
Page 31: Potassium instructions contain source contradictions and stray punctuation; exact wording is retained.
Pages 32–33: Source-visible ‘IVI’ wording is preserved rather than interpreted.
Page 34: Terlipressin route marking conflicts with administration wording; both implicated routes are conditional.
Pages 36–37 include pediatric content inside an adult policy; pediatric rules are intentionally excluded pending a separate approved pediatric protocol.
Pages 36–37: Fentanyl’s adult maximum is printed as ‘1.5 mcg/Kg/hr’ in bolus-dose context and is preserved without correction.
Page 37: Naloxone ‘Maximum dose: 2 mg’ and ‘May repeat every 2-3 minutes’ appear after the Pediatric subsection without a new Adult/shared label; they are not assigned to the adult dose.

proceduralSedationAdult.dose: Adult Age 18-60 years: 1 – 5 mg IV over 5 minutes; titrated in 1 mg per minute increments to a maximum total dose not to exceed 0.2 mg/Kg when used without an opioid. Adult Age > 60 years: 0.5 mg – 1.5 mg IV over 3 minutes titrated in 0.5 mg per minute to a maximum total dose of up to 0.1 mg/Kg when used without an opioid.
proceduralSedationAdult.onsetPeak: Onset of Action: 30 seconds to 1 minute. Peak Effect: 3-5 minutes.
proceduralSedationAdult.sideEffects: Produces anxiolytic, sedative, hypnotic, skeletal muscle relaxant and anticonvulsant effects. Capable of producing all levels of CNS depression from mild sedation to respiratory depression and coma. Anterograde amnesia occurs within 1-5 minutes. Respiratory depression in elderly or when combined with opioids. Hypotension when combined with opioids.

proceduralSedationAdult.duration: 30-60 minutes after a single dose of up to 100 mcg.
proceduralSedationAdult.sideEffects: Respiratory depression increased combined with benzodiazepines. Minimal hypnotic action. Brady/tachy arrhythmias.
